newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria PM says accepts currency board plan.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria PM says accepts currency board plan.

text.p: Bulgaria's Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said on Monday the government and the central bank accepted the currency board plan proposed by the IMF to stabilise the crumbling financial system.

"The government together with the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) plan to inform their partners, the International Monetary Fund, that we have accepted the currency board idea," Videnov told a news conference.
Under the currency board system, the exchange rate is pegged at a fixed level against a hard currency and money in circulation has to correspond to the official hard currency reserves at that rate.
Also, the system deprives the central bank of powers to freely set interest and exchange rates and its authority is replaced by a body that ensureses compliance with the terms.

Videnov said the government was planning to invite an IMF mission for technical preparation of the currency board system which would peg money in ciruculation to the level of hard currency reserves.A later mission would be invited for official negotiations, he added.

By early January the cabinet will prepare and introduce to parliament for approval a package of laws that include the 1997 budget frame and amendments to the central bank law curbing its operations so the currency board can function, said Videnov.
